sections.title: A rebound that did not last

blocks.text: The IHSG fell 3.09% as foreign investors sold a net Rp3.16tn of shares over five days, according to IDX. Thursday alone accounted for Rp1.49tn. The index gained 97.868 points on Wednesday, then lost 133.020 points by Friday. The bounce did not hold, and the selling continued.

sections.title: A weaker rupiah added to the loss

blocks.text: JISDOR rose 0.97% between the two Fridays, so a weaker rupiah added to the loss for an investor measuring returns in dollars without a hedge. JISDOR is set at a different time from the stock market close, so the result is a rough guide, not a return anyone could have locked in.

blocks.text: Only consumer cyclicals ended the week higher, up 0.02%. Industrials fell 5.48%, infrastructure 4.10% and technology 3.96%. These returns show where prices fell. They do not tell us which investors sold.

sections.title: Three stocks accounted for a third of the decline

blocks.text: IDX's index-mover table puts BYAN, BBRI and BMRI together at 66.10 points of the IHSG's net 199.267-point fall. That is about a third of the decline, before gains in other stocks offset some losses.

sections.title: What would make a recovery more convincing

blocks.label: Our stance
blocks.text: Stay cautious. Add exposure in stages only if more sectors join a price recovery and daily foreign selling eases. If you measure returns in dollars without a hedge, check the currency cost against a rate you could actually trade at.
These are things to watch, not forecasts. The levels have not been tested as support or resistance, and we do not put odds on these scenarios.

method: All returns are price returns. Rp bn means billions of rupiah and Rp tn means trillions. IDX marks trades as foreign or domestic using the domicile recorded in its trading system. That does not always tell us who ultimately owns the shares. The dollar return based on JISDOR leaves out dividends, fees, taxes, hedging and tracking costs.
